quiz.q: After `let s2 = s1;` where s1 is a String, what happens to s1?
options: s1 still holds a copy of the string
s1 is moved from and can no longer be used
s1 and s2 share the string and both stay valid
s1 is set to an empty string ""
quiz.explain: For an owning type like String, assignment moves ownership. s1 no longer owns anything, so using it is a compile error.

quiz.q: Why can you still use `x` after `let y = x;` when x is an integer?
options: Integers are special-cased by the compiler
Integers are Copy types, so x is copied, not moved
It's actually a bug and will warn you
Because y is a reference to x
quiz.explain: Small stack values like integers implement Copy, so they are duplicated instead of moved. Both x and y remain valid.

quiz.q: When is a value's memory freed in Rust?
options: When a garbage collector decides to run
When its owner goes out of scope
quiz.explain: Rust drops a value (frees its memory) automatically when the owning variable goes out of scope — no GC, no manual free.

quiz.q: You passed a String into a function and now the compiler says it was 'moved'. What's the cheapest correct fix if you still need it afterward?
options: Call .clone() when passing it, or borrow it with &
quiz.explain: Passing by value moves the String. Clone makes a separate copy; borrowing with & lends it without moving (and is cheaper).

flashcards.back: 1) Each value has one owner. 2) Only one owner at a time. 3) When the owner goes out of scope, the value is dropped (freed).
Assigning or passing an owning value (String, Vec, ...) transfers ownership to the new place. The original variable can no longer be used.

flashcards.front: Which types are copied instead of moved?
flashcards.back: Copy types: simple fixed-size stack values like integers, bool, and char. `let y = x;` copies them, so x stays usable.

flashcards.front: How do you use a value without giving up ownership?
flashcards.back: Borrow it with a reference (&). That lends access without moving, so the original owner keeps the value. (See the Borrowing lesson.)
